native_payload.intent: Fix a race in addrConn where two concurrent connect() calls both saw Idle (mutex released before resetTransport re-acquired it) and started parallel connection attempts. resetTransport becomes resetTransportAndUnlock: callers hold ac.mu and it releases it, so the Connecting transition happens in the same critical section as the Idle check (issue #7365).
residual_risks: updateAddrs now returns with ac.mu still held until the spawned `go ac.resetTransportAndUnlock()` goroutine runs; the deferred `ac.transport.GracefulClose()` (whose onClose needs ac.mu) blocks in that window. The wait is bounded because the goroutine takes no other lock before unlocking, but it adds scheduler latency for anything needing ac.mu (getReadyTransport, getTransport, tearDown, resetConnectBackoff).

The mutex is locked by one goroutine and unlocked by another in updateAddrs. Legal in Go, but a future early return or panic added before the unlock in resetTransportAndUnlock would hold ac.mu forever. All current paths unlock (ctx-error early return; unlock right after the Connecting transition).
Pre-existing, unchanged: with zero addresses tryAllAddrs returns a nil error, so resetTransportAndUnlock takes the success path and leaves the state Connecting.
testing_gaps: No test drives concurrent connect() calls, or connect() racing updateAddrs, and asserts exactly one transport is created; the flaky Test/AuthorityRevive (#7365) is the only coverage of the closed race.
No test covers updateAddrs on a READY subchannel with an active transport under -race (the deferred GracefulClose blocking on ac.mu until the new goroutine unlocks it).
